title: Proteogenomic of postmortem melanoma  metastases from preimmuno
projectDescription: Proteomic analysis of postmortem  melanoma metastases from pre-immunonotherapy era
sampleProcessingProtocol: . Frozen tumor sections (15 of 10 um each) were homogenized and proteins were extrated using a Bioruptor and a lysate buffer consisting of 4M urea in 100 mM Ambic . Protein were enzymaticaly digested overnight using urea in-solution digestion with enzymes Lys-C and trypsin (1:50) . Peptides were C18 desalted and analyzed (1 ug) by LC-MS/MS using an Ultimate 3000 coupled to a Q Exactive HF-X
dataProcessingProtocol: Spectral library building The DIA-MS Spectral library was built out of data dependent acquisition (DDA)-LC-MS/MS analyses using the same LC-MS/MS system as above. Here 24 hpH-RP-HPLC peptide fractions were dissolved in 2% ACN, 0.1% TFA and spiked-in with iRT peptides (Biognosis AG) in a 1:10 dilution (iRT:peptides) (Biognosis AG). The gradient used was the following: 0 min 4% B; 7 min 4% B; 139 min 30% B; 154 min 45% B; 155 min 98% B; 160 min 98% B. The MS parameters were set as follows: selection of the 40 most intense ions for fragmentation, full MS scans at m/z 375-1,750 with a resolution of 120,000 at m/z 200, a target AGC value of 3×106 and IT of 100 ms, fragmentation in HCD collision cell with normalized collision energy (NCE) of 25 and MS/MS spectra acquisition in the Orbitrap analyzer at a resolution of 60,000 (at m/z 200) with a maximum IT of 120 ms and dynamic exclusion of 40 s.   Proteomic data processing for protein quantification For the peptide and protein identification and quantitation in DDA-MS experiments, raw DDA-LC-MS/MS files were analyzed using ProteomeDiscoverer™ Software from Thermo Scientific™ (v 2.3) employing the Uniprot Human protein sequence dataset with isoforms (downloaded 2018-10-01, 70,646 protein entries) using the common proteomics workflows (note: the variant protein sequences inferred based on RNA-Seq were not utilized in these steps, see “Computational pipeline for proteogenomics” in Materials and Methods). The Sequest HT search engine was used for peptide identification, with carbamidomethylation specified as a static modification. Dynamic modifications included oxidation of methionine residues and acetylation at protein N-termini. Precursor and fragment mass tolerances were set at 20 ppm and 0.02 Da, respectively, with allowance for up to two missed cleavages for peptides. Next, a spectral library was generated from the DDA experiments outlined above. Raw files underwent conversion to HTRMS files using a specialized converter provided by Biognosys AG. Subsequently, they were searched within the Spectronaut v11 (Biognosys AG), employing the Homo sapiens database from Uniprot, inclusive of isoforms (downloaded 2018-10-01, 70,646 protein entries) (note: the variant protein sequences inferred based on RNA-Seq were not utilized in these steps either, see “Computational pipeline for proteogenomics” in Materials and Methods). Dynamic retention time prediction was chosen to facilitate nonlinear alignment of precursor retention times between the (iRT, normalized retention time) spectral library and the DIA-MS data through segmented regression. The following search parameters were employed: cysteine carbamidomethylation (+57.0215 Da) as a fixed modification, and methionine oxidation (+15.9949 Da) along with N-terminal acetylation (+42.0105 Da) as dynamic modifications. Up to two missed cleavages were permitted. Precursor mass tolerance was set to 10 ppm, while for the MS/MS fragments, it was set to 0.02 Da. Between 3 and 25 fragments were collected per peptide. Filtering was conducted at a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) for all peptides and proteins utilized in constructing the spectral library. The software calculated MS1 peptide abundance as the sum of precursor XIC (Extracted-Ion Chromatogram) from the monoisotopic precursor ion and its isotopic envelope. Protein abundance was derived from the average of the top three most intense precursor ions corresponding to unique and razor peptides.
